[L5] **Explicit local integral data.** With $a=a_{\mu}$, the Kummer regular solutions for $(n,l)=(1,0),(2,1)$ have $j=n-l-1=0$, $L_{0}^{(1)}=L_{0}^{(3)}=1$, decay rates $1/a,1/(2a)$, and normalized positive radial representatives $u_{10}=2a^{-3/2}r e^{-r/a}$, $u_{21}=(2\sqrt6)^{-1}a^{-5/2}r^{2}e^{-r/(2a)}$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-kummer-recurrence-and-termination]] clauses (c)-(e)). Their normalizations follow locally from $\int_0^{\infty}r^{k}e^{-br}dr=k!/b^{k+1}$ ([[lem-nrqm-central-exponential-moments]]). The sphere family is orthonormal with the positive real representatives $Y_{00}=1/\sqrt{4\pi}$, $Y_{10}=\sqrt{3/(4\pi)}\,\Omega_{3}$, obtained from $P_{0}=1$, $P_{1}=t$ and the normalizing integral ([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] clauses (c), (e), [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]); sphere integration is $d\sigma=\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$ ([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]]). ex-nrqm-approximations-stark-finite-leve.before: 1.1 [The compressed matrices] By [L2], each $D^{W}_{j}$ is a compression of a self-adjoint operator to $W$, hence a Hermitian $2\times2$ matrix with unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$; the diagonal entries $\langle\psi_{1},D_{j}\psi_{1}\rangle$ and $\langle\psi_{2},D_{j}\psi_{2}\rangle$ factor into a radial integral times an angular integral with $l'=l$, which vanishes by the selection rule; and the off-diagonal entries factor with angular labels $(l,m)=(0,0)$, $(l',m')=(1,0)$, for which only the component $q=0$, that is $D_{3}$, can contribute. Choosing the phase of $\psi_{2}$ so that the surviving number is real and positive gives $D^{W}_{1}=D^{W}_{2}=0$ and $D^{W}_{3}=D_{\rm rel}\sigma_{1}$ with $D_{\rm rel}=|\langle\psi_{2},D_{3}\psi_{1}\rangle|>0$, to be read as a model parameter. This is clause (a). [L2, given, algebra]
ex-nrqm-approximations-stark-finite-leve.after: 1.1 [The compressed matrices and their nonzero entry] Write $a=a_{\mu}$. From [L5], $\|u_{10}\|_{2}^{2}=4a^{-3}2!/(2/a)^{3}=1$ and $\|u_{21}\|_{2}^{2}=(24a^{5})^{-1}4!/(1/a)^{5}=1$; the explicit Kummer solutions therefore give the normalized bound states with the stated labels. For their positive real representatives, $\int_{S^{2}}Y_{10}\Omega_{3}Y_{00}\,d\sigma=(\sqrt3/(4\pi))2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}t^{2}dt=1/\sqrt3$. Their radial dipole integral is $\int_{0}^{\infty}r u_{21}u_{10}\,dr=(1/\sqrt6)a^{-4}4!/(3/(2a))^{5}=256a/(81\sqrt6)>0$. The absolutely convergent factorization [L2] yields $\langle\psi_{210},Q_{3}\psi_{100}\rangle=128\sqrt2 a/243>0$. Since $D_{3}=-qQ_{3}$, its matrix element is $-128\sqrt2 q a/243$ before rephasing. Set $\psi_{1}=\psi_{100}$ and $\psi_{2}=-\psi_{210}$ to obtain the positive off-diagonal value $D_{\rm rel}=128\sqrt2 q a/243$ without changing energies, labels or normalization. By [L2], bound states lie in all coordinate domains; all diagonal entries vanish by degree selection, and the off-diagonal $Q_{\pm}$ entries vanish by weight selection. Thus $D^{W}_{1}=D^{W}_{2}=0$ and $D^{W}_{3}=D_{\rm rel}\sigma_{1}$ with $D_{\rm rel}>0$, proving (a). [L1, L2, L5, given, algebra]

ex-nrqm-approximations-stark-finite-leve.before: 3.1 [The finite remainder check] At $\mathcal E=\Delta/(16D_{\rm rel})$ one has $\lambda v=\Delta/8$, so $|\lambda|=R/2$ with $R=\Delta/(8v)$, and the page's bound gives $Rv(1/2)^{3}/(1-1/2)=Rv/4=\Delta/32$. The exact lower branch is $$F_{-}=\frac{E_{1}+E_{2}}{2}-\frac{\Delta}{2}\sqrt{1+\tfrac1{16}} =E_{1}+\frac{\Delta}{2}-\frac{\Delta\sqrt{17}}{8} =E_{1}-\frac{\Delta(\sqrt{17}-4)}{8},$$ while the second-order truncation is $E_{1}+\lambda^{2}E''(0)/2=E_{1}-\Delta/64$; the exact remainder is therefore $$\Bigl|F_{-}-E_{1}+\frac{\Delta}{64}\Bigr| =\Delta\Bigl|\frac{1}{64}-\frac{\sqrt{17}-4}{8}\Bigr| =\Delta\,\frac{33-8\sqrt{17}}{64},$$ which by [L4] is $\approx2.37\cdot10^{-4}\Delta\le\Delta/32$; the comparison is exact algebra. This is clause (d). [L3, L4, step 2.1, algebra]
ex-nrqm-approximations-stark-finite-leve.after: 3.1 [The finite remainder check at the true half radius] At $\mathcal E=\Delta/(16D_{\rm rel})$, $\lambda v=D_{\rm rel}\mathcal E=\Delta/16$ and hence $\lambda=R/2$ for $R=\Delta/(8v)$. The page's bound is $Rv(1/2)^{3}/(1-1/2)=Rv/4=\Delta/32$. The exact lower branch satisfies $F_{-}=E_{1}+\Delta/2-\sqrt{\Delta^{2}/4+\Delta^{2}/256}=E_{1}+\Delta(8-\sqrt{65})/16$, whereas its quadratic truncation is $E_{1}-(\lambda v)^{2}/\Delta=E_{1}-\Delta/256$. Therefore $|F_{-}-E_{1}+\Delta/256|=\Delta(129-16\sqrt{65})/256=\Delta/[256(129+16\sqrt{65})]$ by [L4]. Since $129+16\sqrt{65}>128$, this remainder is strictly less than $\Delta/32768$, and consequently less than $\Delta/32$. This proves (d) without a decimal approximation. [L3, L4, step 2.1, algebra]
